_README: EXPECTED-RED LEDGER. Every gate that is RED must appear here with a
MEASURED watermark, an owner and a review_by date. This is what lets CI
ask 'is anything red that we did not already record, or REDDER than we
recorded?' instead of 'is anything red?', which was a constant and
This ledger SOFTENS NOTHING. The gates still print RED, first, on every
run. What it changes is the exit code, so a NEW break is distinguishable
- a RED gate not listed here      -> FAIL (it is new)
- a RED gate worse than watermark -> FAIL (it regressed)
- a GREEN gate still listed here  -> FAIL (stale; delete the entry)
- past review_by                  -> FAIL (re-measure or sign an extension)
review_by is the anti-wallpaper clause: an expected-red gate must not

Gate 6R.metric: dated editions recorded in navalai/rules/review.py REVIEW['editions']
Gate 6R.bar: every implemented standard named with the DATED edition the reviewer held, e.g. 'ISO 12217-1:2022'
Gate 6R.measured_on: navalai/rules/review.py, both entries read 'edition not recorded — set this'
Gate 6R.verify: python -m pytest tests/test_phase6r.py -q  (and: python -c "from navalai.rules.review import edition_defects; print(edition_defects())")
why_red: GAP D8. This gate WAS GREEN, and it should not have been. review.py's
own docstring states 'a confirmation that cannot say WHO checked WHICH
edition is not a review, it is a rumour' — and then is_complete()
checked `reviewer` and `confirmed` and NOT `editions`, whose two values
both read 'edition not recorded — set this'. The parity gate was green
on a record that admits in its own field values that it cannot name the
document it checked.
is_complete() now requires every edition to be set and to carry a year.
That FLIPPED THIS GATE RED on 2026-08-06. Under honesty rule 6 that is
the correct outcome and not a regression: the check got stricter, the
underlying state did not get worse. Nothing was softened to absorb it —
the row prints RED, first, on every run.
CLEARING CONDITION, and it costs no compute: a reviewer writes the two
dated editions into REVIEW['editions'], deletes this entry, and flips
the row in navalai/gates.py. tests/test_phase6r.py already asserts that
a properly filled record completes, so the clearing condition is
executable rather than prose.
AND NOTE WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT ANSWER (gap D9). Its scope is
THRESHOLD parity: does our number equal the standard's number.
BuildPlan Gate 6's bar is VERDICT parity — the same verdict as a
qualified reviewer on at least three reference designs, hand
calculated. Zero reference designs and zero hand calculations exist,
and the reviewer of record is the project owner reviewing his own code
with no qualification recorded. Clearing 6R does not open Gate 6.
Gate 6R-mech is a SEPARATE, GREEN row: the mechanics around the record
(basis routing, no unreviewed basis leaking 'standard', our own
practice values not blessed by a green gate) are genuinely verified.

Gate 2U.metric: % of a random valid-hull batch that meshes AND converges unattended
why_red: 2 of 8 sampled valid hulls produced zero-volume cells or wrongly
oriented faces, both fatal to interFoam on timestep 1. BuildPlan Risk
#1 is now a number instead of a worry.
N=8 is a small sample and the watermark should be read as such. The
'converges' half of the bar has NEVER been measured: --solve exists and
has not been run, so today's 75% is a MESHING rate only.
